runs.text: Every move sends one peg strictly to the right, so the sum of occupied hole numbers strictly increases and is bounded. Therefore the game always terminates. A strategy that guarantees a legal response after every opponent move must eventually make the final move.

A pairing strategy partitions objects into fixed pairs and answers a move involving one member by making the corresponding move with its partner. The proof must verify that the partner source remains occupied, the partner destination remains vacant, and the response obeys the direction rule.

Call a configuration good if each pair contains either two pegs or no pegs. Since
is even, the starting configuration is good.

Suppose Alice moves from a good configuration. Her source lies in a full pair and her destination in an empty pair. Bob moves the other peg of the source pair to the other hole of the destination pair. This is legal: Alice's destination is to the right of her source, so the entire destination pair is to the right of the entire source pair. Bob's move restores a good configuration.
